- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- If recent events show high bearish supply net (e.g., >-15) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid overestimating rebound.
- After a sharp spike in true outcome (e.g., >+10% from prior day), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast increase to +5% per day to avoid lagged overreaction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00s), model should not forecast a flat trend — expect mean reversion within 5–7 days unless policy event overrides.
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low (≤0.33), forecast should be conservative — avoid upward drift; target 1–2% below recent 18-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 18-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent volatility — don’t assume linear continuation.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (e.g., 3+ alternating 0.00/1.00), model should not forecast smooth trend — expect ±3% noise around 18-day average.
